findings.name: three.js (r186 / npm 0.186.1)
findings.what_it_does: Core WebGL/WebGPU 3D engine. r186 adds SunLight (WebGPU), SSAO/GTAO/OIT nodes, Gaussian splats. Hub that R3F, That Open, Speckle viewer and the Rhino 3dm loader all build on.
findings.how_we_use_it: Pin 0.186.x with the WebGL2 renderer as the viewport. Use built-in loaders (OBJ, glTF, 3DM), clipping planes and CSM shadows. Keep the renderer behind a thin adapter so WebGPU can be adopted later.
findings.saves: Biggest ecosystem; Claude knows its API well (expected, not measured), so fewer tokens on docs and fixes.
findings.risks: Releases deprecate APIs (r186 removed PCFSoftShadowMap and minified builds); @types/three lags TSL; WebGPU path still maturing.
findings.popularity: 116.7k stars, 36.7k forks; GitHub API shows 393 open issues+PRs
findings.last_activity: Pushed 2026-10-21; r186 released 2026-09-24 (verified via GitHub API/npm on 21 Oct 2026)

findings.name: react-three-fiber (R3F) v9.8.2
findings.what_it_does: React renderer for three.js. v9 targets React 19. v10 alpha (alpha.6, 2026-10-17) makes WebGPU the default renderer and moves TSL hooks to @react-three/tsl.
findings.how_we_use_it: Build the viewport and node-canvas 3D previews declaratively. Pin R3F 9.8.x with react 19.3.x. Use frameloop="demand" so idle scenes cost nothing. Do not adopt v10 alpha for the 13 Nov core.
findings.saves: Declarative scene code is shorter for Claude to write and review; drei supplies most helpers.
findings.risks: Peer range react >=19 <19.4 limits upgrades; v10 changes renderer defaults and GLSL libraries need a legacy entry; some community add-ons are stale (@react-three/a11y last 2022).

findings.name: @react-three/drei 10.7.9
findings.what_it_does: Helper library for R3F: Edges (EdgesGeometry, default 15 degree threshold), Outlines (inverted hull), Line (Line2 fat lines), CameraControls, PerformanceMonitor, Bvh, Html, Grid, Sky, AccumulativeShadows, SoftShadows.
findings.how_we_use_it: Main viewport toolbox. Edges plus Line for thin architectural linework; Outlines for hover/selection; CameraControls for saved camera bookmarks; PerformanceMonitor to adapt DPR on weak laptops; Html for in-scene labels.
findings.saves: Replaces weeks of custom helpers; documented components keep prompts short.
findings.risks: Some docs are thin (Sky props not fully visible); 139 open issues+PRs; tied to R3F 9 and React 19; Edges per-mesh lines can add draw calls on big context models.

findings.name: pmndrs/postprocessing 6.39.5 + @react-three/postprocessing 3.2.1
findings.what_it_does: WebGL post-processing: Outline, SSAO, SMAA, tone mapping, depth. The R3F wrapper also lists Kuwahara (painterly), Halftone, Linocut and Ramp effects usable for diagrammatic or non-photorealistic looks.
findings.how_we_use_it: Default chain: SMAA, tone mapping, selection Outline. Optional presentation presets (halftone/Kuwahara) for board diagrams. Add N8AO through its postprocessing pass; the wrapper's effect list does not include it.
findings.saves: Ready-made effects instead of hand-written shaders.
findings.risks: Peer range three >=0.168 <0.187 blocks upgrading three past 0.186; v7 still alpha/beta; WebGPU not mentioned in README.

findings.name: N8AO 2.0.1
findings.what_it_does: Ambient-occlusion pass for three.js with quality presets, optional neural denoise, half-resolution mode (README claims 2x-4x speedup), accumulation for still cameras, and a postprocessing pass.
findings.how_we_use_it: Default AO for the clay-massing look. Use half-resolution plus still-camera accumulation on laptops; switch off in the Low quality tier. Wrap N8AOPostPass in our own R3F component.
findings.saves: Strong depth cues for the cost of one pass, no custom AO code.
findings.risks: WebGL2 only; README says not yet WebGPU-compatible. README licence CC0-1.0 but npm lists ISC (check before shipping). 503 stars, one maintainer. Speedup figures are vendor claims.

findings.name: three-mesh-bvh 0.9.16
findings.what_it_does: Bounding-volume hierarchy for fast raycasts and spatial queries on three.js meshes; async/worker builds, BatchedMesh support, GPU SDF and path-tracing examples. Foundation for three-edge-projection and three-bvh-csg.
findings.how_we_use_it: Fast picking on large context meshes and imported BIM. Cast rays from grid points toward the sun for solar-access and shadow-hour analysis modules without a GPU readback.
findings.saves: Avoids writing spatial indexing; one dependency covers picking and analysis.
findings.risks: README performance claim (500 rays on 80k polygons at 60 fps) is untested on student laptops; BVH build time on huge IFC models; essentially one maintainer.

findings.name: Manifold (manifold-3d 3.5.4)
findings.what_it_does: Guaranteed-manifold mesh boolean library in WASM. d.ts confirms extrude with twist and scaleTop, slice(height) to CrossSection, area(), volume(), surfaceArea(), project(), splitByPlane, trimByPlane, hull, offset.
findings.how_we_use_it: Run in a worker as the massing kernel: floorplate stacks (twist/taper/setbacks), podium plus tower unions, site subtractions, per-floor GFA via slice().area(), volume, footprint via project(), section cuts via splitByPlane.
findings.saves: One robust kernel for massing, areas and sections; avoids heavy B-rep WASM (about 2.8 MB unpacked package).
findings.risks: Triangle meshes only, no NURBS; inputs must be manifold; WASM build is serial-only; STL export discouraged; manual memory cleanup in JS; imported Rhino/IFC meshes may need repair.
findings.popularity: 2.4k stars, 272 forks; used by OpenSCAD, Blender, Godot, Babylon.js per README

findings.name: rhino3dm.js 8.35.0 + three Rhino3dmLoader
findings.what_it_does: openNURBS compiled to WASM: read/write .3dm, create geometry containers (breps, meshes, SubD), client for Rhino Compute. three.js ships Rhino3dmLoader that decodes in web workers and meshes SubD.
findings.how_we_use_it: Import .3dm massing through Rhino3dmLoader, with the wasm hosted locally rather than from a CDN. Optionally write a simple massing back to .3dm so Rhino users can round-trip.
findings.saves: Direct Rhino import with no server; avoids a custom parser.
findings.risks: README lists no booleans or meshing; advanced ops need Rhino Compute (server, cost). Loader docs pin 8.32.1 but npm is 8.35.0. Breps without stored render meshes are untested.

findings.name: web-ifc 0.0.78
findings.what_it_does: C++ IFC reader/writer compiled to WASM for browser and Node, with a multithreaded build. Reads and writes IFC at what the README calls native speeds; npm package web-ifc.
findings.how_we_use_it: Import IFC massing and context into the viewport. Write IFC from our tagged massing (storeys, spaces) for Revit hand-off. Run in a worker.
findings.saves: Replaces a custom IFC parser; same engine that That Open and many viewers use.
findings.risks: MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft, fine for open source). Version 0.0.x pre-1.0; README states no schema versions (IFC2x3/IFC4/IFC4x3) or benchmarks; edge-case geometry unverified.

findings.name: That Open Engine: @thatopen/components 3.4.9 + fragments 3.4.8
findings.what_it_does: MIT toolkit for BIM apps on three.js: floorplan navigation, dimensions, DXF export (README), plus Fragments, a FlatBuffers binary BIM format claimed to handle millions of elements in seconds. Peers: three >=0.182, web-ifc >=0.0.77.
findings.how_we_use_it: v1 IFC panel: clipper, plan views and element picking for imported Revit/IFC. Use Fragments for large models. Load lazily so it does not weigh down the massing path.
findings.saves: Section/plan/measure tooling for imported BIM without custom code.
findings.risks: Fast-moving 3.x with docs gaps (component list not confirmed from README); performance claims untested; extra bundle weight; learning curve beyond plain three.js.

findings.name: xeokit-sdk 2.6.114
findings.what_it_does: Pure-WebGL 3D BIM/IFC viewer SDK with double precision and an XKT pre-converted format; plugins for glTF, CityJSON, LAS. Not built on three.js. Commercial licence sold by Creoox.
findings.how_we_use_it: Do not embed. Study its XKT and double-precision ideas only. Revisit only if the platform itself is released under AGPL-3.0.
findings.saves: Nothing for our stack; avoids a licence trap.
findings.risks: AGPL-3.0 forces integrated code open under AGPL; separate renderer duplicates our viewport; ES5/UMD builds being dropped; 191 open issues.

findings.name: Speckle viewer (@speckle/viewer 2.31.14)
findings.what_it_does: Apache-2.0 three.js extension for viewing Speckle data. Docs state Viewer 2 cannot render current parquet-bundle model versions without a bridge, and Viewer 3 is unreleased.
findings.how_we_use_it: Not in core. Possible later import path for Revit, Rhino or SketchUp users via Speckle connectors, loading data into our own viewport rather than using their viewer.
findings.saves: Potential Revit/SketchUp connector reuse later.
findings.risks: Viewer API in flux; requires Speckle server for data; repo licence can vary per folder (GitHub shows NOASSERTION); last viewer publish 2026-06-15.

findings.name: replicad + replicad-opencascadejs 1.1.0
findings.what_it_does: Code-CAD library for the browser on an OpenCascade WASM build. Sketch, extrude, fillet, booleans and STEP/STL export per its tags and docs; web workbench at studio.replicad.xyz.
findings.how_we_use_it: v1 detail module for B-rep parts (facade brackets, connection details) and STEP export, in a worker. Not used for tower massing, where Manifold is lighter.
findings.saves: Maintained OCCT build and API; avoids building opencascade.js ourselves.
findings.risks: One maintainer, 706 stars. WASM package is LGPL-2.1 and about 48.8 MB unpacked incl. builds. README did not confirm feature list, worker setup or wasm size.

findings.name: occt-wasm 5.7.1
findings.what_it_does: OpenCascade 8.0.1 as WASM with a TypeScript API: booleans, fillet, chamfer, shell, sweeps, STEP/STL/glTF export, OcctWorker. About 4.5 MB brotli, roughly half opencascade.js per README.
findings.how_we_use_it: Watch only. Candidate replacement kernel for B-rep detail modules after 10 Dec if replicad proves heavy or stale. Prototype one module behind a flag, not in core.
findings.saves: Smaller download if it matures.
findings.risks: First npm release 2026-03-27; one maintainer; 65 stars; manual shape release; needs WASM SIMD, tail calls and exception handling; no IGES; LGPL-2.1 WASM.
findings.license: MIT or Apache-2.0 tooling; WASM LGPL-2.1

findings.name: opencascade.js 1.1.1
findings.what_it_does: Original OCCT-to-WASM port (OCCT 7.6.2 badge). GitHub last pushed 2023-08-15; npm latest 1.1.1 dated 2020-09-27 and modified 2023-03-23. Replicad ships its own custom build.
findings.how_we_use_it: Do not adopt. Use replicad-opencascadejs or occt-wasm if a B-rep kernel is needed.
findings.saves: Avoids a stale dependency and its heavy build chain.
findings.risks: Unmaintained since 2023; about 9 MB wasm (per occt-wasm README); LGPL-2.1; 77 open issues.

findings.name: CadQuery and build123d (Python B-rep)
findings.what_it_does: Python parametric B-rep libraries on OCP/OpenCASCADE, with STEP export. CadQuery pip supports Python 3.9-3.12 per README; build123d lists 3.11-3.14. Neither is in the Pyodide 314.0.7 package list.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap only: an optional local Python worker for STEP export. Not a browser path. Prefer Manifold or replicad in-browser.
findings.saves: None now; avoids chasing a Pyodide route that does not exist in the official package list.
findings.risks: Native OCP wheels can be blocked on Windows 11 with Smart App Control (per text-to-cad README); Python 3.13 mismatch for CadQuery pip; students need installs.
findings.last_activity: Not shown on pages; not checked

findings.name: earthtojake/text-to-cad
findings.what_it_does: Plugin with 12 agent skills (CAD, DXF, drawings, URDF, DfAM, DFM, G-code) and a local MCP server (cadgen mcp) on build123d 0.11 and OCCT 7.9. Outputs STEP/STL/3MF/GLB; includes a local CAD viewer; installs in Claude Code.
findings.how_we_use_it: Dev-time Claude Code plugin for small mechanical details (brackets, connectors). Copy its packaging pattern (skills, local MCP, viewer) for our module-authoring skill. Not for tower massing.
findings.saves: Ready CAD skills; its packaging pattern saves designing our own agent interface.
findings.risks: No architecture-scale examples; telemetry on by default (opt out with uvx cadgen telemetry off); Smart App Control blocks OCP on Windows 11; needs uv, Python 3.11+, Node 20+; first run downloads runtime.
findings.last_activity: Commit date not shown (GitHub API returned 403)

findings.name: Zoo Design Studio / Text-to-CAD (KittyCAD modeling-app)
findings.what_it_does: MIT desktop CAD app storing models as KCL code. README says the 3D view streams from Zoo's hosted geometry engine. Text-to-CAD/Zookeeper is a hosted service on monthly usage credits; @kittycad/kcl-wasm-lib is MIT.
findings.how_we_use_it: Not core. Optional API behind a feature flag later for mechanical parts. Do not depend on it for towers or offline use.
findings.saves: Nothing for the core path.
findings.risks: Hosted engine dependency and usage cost; no published benchmarks (marketing claims only); pricing tiers not visible; KCL licence and local execution not confirmed.

findings.name: LLM-to-CAD research: Text-to-CadQuery, CADCodeVerify, cad0
findings.what_it_does: Text-to-CadQuery: best of six fine-tuned LLMs reached 69.3% top-1 exact match on an augmented Text2CAD set. CADCodeVerify (2410.05340): visual self-checks gave +5.0% success with GPT-4 on 200 prompts. cad0 reports 75% in-distribution, weak out-of-distribution.
findings.how_we_use_it: Evidence for a constrained text-to-massing design: LLM emits JSON parameters for our massing nodes, we render and verify, then a human edits. No free-form CAD generation in core.
findings.saves: Prevents spending build time on unreliable free-form text-to-CAD; JSON generation is cheap in tokens.
findings.risks: Benchmarks are single mechanical parts, not towers; numbers come from papers and are not reproduced by us; a blog source cites dimension drift without data.
findings.maintainer: Xie and Ju (Text-to-CadQuery); Alrashedy et al. (CADCodeVerify); campedersen (cad0)

findings.name: Hairline (lucasmarkes/hairline, npm 0.5.1)
findings.what_it_does: 33 pointer-responsive isometric line figures as dependency-free SVG with a React entry. Six theme tokens (plate, hi, edge, mid, lo, stroke width 0.9px), one shared animation loop that sleeps when idle, reduced-motion support, plus hairline-create and hairline-adopt agent skills.
findings.how_we_use_it: Use tokens and rules for UI illustrations, module-card thumbnails, empty states and onboarding. Apply the same plate/edge/mid/lo ladder to 3D viewport colours. Generate custom figures with hairline-create sparingly.
findings.saves: Ready-made calm visual language; skills avoid hand-drawing icons.
findings.risks: Needs a DOM (no SSR); plate colour set by hand on non-default backgrounds; About text says six figures vs README 33; commit date not shown; X post praising it is a single unverified voice.

findings.name: Anatomy (wheresryan22/anatomy)
findings.what_it_does: MIT agent skill that turns a concept into an interactive isometric machine in shaded SVG with optional WebGL shaders and a beta 3D mode. Node 20.10+, no runtime dependencies; documented example took about 1 h 54 min of agent time.
findings.how_we_use_it: Use for one or two hero explainers (landing page, onboarding), not per module. Borrow its audit idea (headless-Chrome geometry checks) and light-theme-first craft rules for our own figures.
findings.saves: Hero illustrations without a designer, at a high one-off cost.
findings.risks: Slow and token-heavy by design (author says substantial, no figures); non-deterministic outputs; 3D mode beta; created 2026-10-08 so very young; abstract ideas give labelled boxes.

findings.name: three-edge-projection
findings.what_it_does: Projects visible mesh edges along the Y axis into 2D line segments with a silhouette generator, built on three-mesh-bvh. Step-based generator can spread work across frames. README does not mention SVG or section lines.
findings.how_we_use_it: v1 hidden-line plan and roof views for board figure-ground drawings. Use Manifold slice for section and floor-plan polygons instead.
findings.saves: Hidden-line projection without writing a rasteriser.
findings.risks: Y-axis only per README; installs from GitHub rather than npm (npm lookup failed); 354 stars; 12 open issues; no benchmarks.

findings.name: three.js CSM addon and SunLight
findings.what_it_does: CSM (cascaded shadow maps) works only with WebGLRenderer and splits the view frustum into cascades for large scenes. SunLight (r186 addon) is documented for WebGPURenderer with SunLightShadow cascades.
findings.how_we_use_it: Use CSM with a directional light placed from the SunCalc sun vector for crisp shadows across a block and tower in the WebGL viewport. Adopt SunLight when we move to WebGPU.
findings.saves: Built-in large-scene shadows; no custom cascade code.
findings.risks: Defaults need tuning (3 cascades, 2048 maps); every material needs csm.setupMaterial; heavy on integrated GPUs, so Low tier should drop to one map. SunLight WebGL support unconfirmed.

findings.name: SunCalc (mourner/suncalc) 2.1.1
findings.what_it_does: Dependency-free JS for sun position (altitude and azimuth via getPosition(date, lat, lng)) and sun times; v2 is a precision rewrite. README says azimuth is clockwise from north.
findings.how_we_use_it: Drive viewport sun direction and the sun/shadow module for Vancouver (49.28 N). Wrap in one function with unit tests against known solstice and equinox values to lock the convention.
findings.saves: Tiny, well known; no astronomy code to write.
findings.risks: README says BSD-2-Clause but npm 2.1.1 licence field is blank; v2 changed behaviour versus v1 (azimuth convention); verify with tests. Time-zone/DST handling is on us.

findings.name: three.js clipping plus stencil caps (section-cut technique)
findings.what_it_does: Official example: WebGLRenderer with stencil:true and localClippingEnabled; back faces increment, front faces decrement the stencil; a cap quad drawn where stencil is nonzero fills the cut, repositioned each frame on the plane.
findings.how_we_use_it: Implement the section-cut preset: movable section planes with solid poche caps on the massing. Combine with orthographic camera and thin Edges for the architectural section look.
findings.saves: Proven recipe; avoids geometry-based capping on every slider move.
findings.risks: Needs closed (watertight) meshes for correct caps; one cap pass per plane; WebGL-specific, so WebGPU port later; hatching still needs separate shader or Manifold slice.

findings.name: three-cad-viewer 5.1.3
findings.what_it_does: MIT three.js CAD viewer with navigation tree, explode, orthographic toggle, black edges, transparency, clipping stencils and part updates. Depends on n8ao, postprocessing and three. Takes its own shapes JSON.
findings.how_we_use_it: Reference implementation for explode, edge colouring and tree UI built on the same N8AO/postprocessing stack. Borrow patterns; do not embed wholesale.
findings.saves: Working example of explode plus AO plus edges, so Claude can copy patterns.
findings.risks: Custom input format; README does not document measurement or clipping details; small (395 stars); one maintainer.

findings.name: takram three-geospatial (three-atmosphere)
findings.what_it_does: MIT monorepo: precomputed atmospheric scattering (beta), volumetric clouds (beta), core and effects (alpha). Active rewrite to a node-based WebGPU API that will be incompatible with the current one.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap for a photoreal sky in presentation mode. For now use drei Sky or three Sky; do not take a dependency before the API settles.
findings.saves: Realistic sky later without custom atmosphere shaders.
findings.risks: Beta/alpha parts and a breaking API rewrite; sun-position and 3D Tiles are not features of this repo; check Google 3D Tiles terms separately.

findings.name: Babylon.js 9.31.2
findings.what_it_does: Apache-2.0 full 3D engine with tooling, viewer package and exporters. Very active; uses Manifold for CSG per Manifold README.
findings.how_we_use_it: Reject as the viewport engine: our importers, R3F helpers and BIM tooling target three.js. Revisit only if we need its tooling.
findings.saves: Avoids splitting effort across two engines.
findings.risks: Ecosystem mismatch (That Open, rhino3dm loader, drei); migration cost; fewer architecture-specific examples found in this pass.

findings.name: Theatre.js (@theatre/core 0.7.2)
findings.what_it_does: Animation library with a visual studio. Core is Apache-2.0; @theatre/studio is AGPL-3.0. README says development moved to a private repo for v1.0; public repo last pushed 2024-08-14; npm 0.7.2 dated 2024-05-19.
findings.how_we_use_it: Do not adopt. For camera tours and exploded-floor animations use drei CameraControls plus our own spring/tween code following Hairline's interaction rules.
findings.saves: Avoids a stale dependency and AGPL tooling.
findings.risks: Stalled public development; AGPL studio package must never ship; 141 open issues; future 1.0 licence unknown.

findings.name: xunliuDesign GitHub account
findings.what_it_does: Xun Liu's account lists 15 public repos. Relevant: false-creek-2100 (pixel sea-level-rise sandbox for South False Creek, plain JS with no build step; code licence not stated) and AI4GH (C# GenAI-in-Grasshopper components incl. Nano Banana_GH). The three named tools are not in this list.
findings.how_we_use_it: Read false-creek-2100 as a Vancouver-specific engagement-UX reference (paint tools, PNG export with metrics, disclaimer framing). Check AI4GH for how Xun wires image APIs into Grasshopper.
findings.saves: Course-aligned precedent and local context for tone and data sources.
findings.risks: No stated code licence on false-creek-2100; AI4GH has 5 commits and no visible README body; hairline, anatomy and text-to-cad belong to other authors.
findings.license: Not stated for the relevant repos

principles.principle: Pin a WebGL2 stack now, plan WebGPU later. The ecosystem is split: R3F v10 alpha is WebGPU-first, while postprocessing (three <0.187) and N8AO are WebGL-only and SunLight is WebGPU-only.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Lock three 0.186.x, R3F 9.8.x, drei 10.7.x, react 19.3.x. Put the renderer behind one adapter module and avoid GLSL-only dependencies outside it. Re-evaluate WebGPU after 10 Dec.

principles.principle: Render only when something changes, and degrade quality gracefully. R3F docs recommend on-demand frames, instancing, and PerformanceMonitor-driven DPR.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Use frameloop="demand", PerformanceMonitor for adaptive DPR, instancing for repeated facade or floor elements, and accumulate AO and soft shadows only when the camera rests. Offer Low/Medium/High tiers the user can override.

principles.principle: Keep lines thin and calm. In Anatomy's craft rules the boldest tone is for the subject, secondary edges are fainter, and every line lands on a real edge or fades.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Viewport linework: 1 to 1.5 px fat lines from Edges (15 degree threshold), silhouette darker than internal edges, context lighter still. No dashed or blueprint clutter in the default view; put dimensions in the legend/inspector.

principles.principle: Monochrome with one lit accent keeps attention and makes meaningful colour stand out. Anatomy and Hairline both reserve colour for the subject.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Default clay-and-hairline palette plus a single accent for selection and hover. Reserve the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour and analysis false-colour ramps so no UI chrome uses them (our inference from these rules).

principles.principle: Design light theme first and define every colour as a token with light and dark values; filled plates hide what is behind them. Hairline exposes plate, hi, edge, mid, lo and stroke-width tokens.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Map viewport and UI colours to a token ladder (plate/hi/edge/mid/lo/accent). Never darken a glow for dark mode; define separate dark values. Set the plate token to the viewport background.

principles.principle: Interaction polish that respects attention: hit areas stay still, springs for continuous values and short eased tweens for discrete picks, one lit accent, a designed rest pose, the loop sleeps when idle, reach is clamped, reduced motion jumps to end state.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Apply to explode sliders, camera bookmarks and node hover. Test picking against the target pose, not the moving pose. No autoplay beyond user-started tours; respect prefers-reduced-motion. This keeps engagement honest, with no dark patterns.

principles.principle: Use the right edge technique per job: EdgesGeometry lines for crisp permanent linework (a forum thread of 5 replies reports it works, a single voice); inverted-hull Outlines for hover and selection; post-process Outline for selected groups.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Edges for all massing and context, Outlines (screenspace thickness) for hover, postprocessing Outline for multi-select. Avoid whole-scene screen-space edge detection in the default look: it costs a pass and is noisy.

principles.principle: Section cuts are a stencil-plus-clipping recipe, and plan/section drawing geometry should come from the mesh kernel, not the render pass.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Viewport sections: clipping planes plus stencil caps (needs watertight meshes). Board drawings: Manifold slice(height) polygons to SVG for poche and floor plans; three-edge-projection for hidden-line roof/plan views (Y-axis only).

principles.principle: For towers, mesh kernels beat B-rep kernels: massing needs extrude, twist, taper, booleans, area and volume. B-rep WASM is large (opencascade.js about 9 MB, occt-wasm about 4.5 MB brotli) and mainly serves detail parts.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Massing nodes run on Manifold in a worker and report volume, GFA per floor and surface area. Offer replicad/occt-wasm only as optional v1 detail modules loaded on demand.

principles.principle: Heavy kernels and parsers belong in web workers, with manual memory management. Rhino3dmLoader decodes in workers; occt-wasm provides OcctWorker and requires release(); Manifold objects need explicit cleanup.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: One kernel worker pool with a typed message API. Each node result carries a dispose hook. Show a progress/cancel affordance for long operations so the canvas never freezes.

principles.principle: AI geometry generation is unreliable for free-form CAD and is trained on mechanical parts. Reported figures: 69.3% exact match for a fine-tuned model on single parts, +5% from visual feedback. Vendor claims for Zoo have no published benchmarks.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Text-to-massing: the LLM returns JSON against a typed massing schema (footprint, height, setbacks, twist, program split); we validate with Manifold (positive volume, manifold, bounds), render, and let the user edit parameters. Log every AI output as an editable team assumption.

principles.principle: Make the 3D canvas accessible with a synced semantic DOM beside it, keyboard operation, status announcements and reduced motion (a forum thread with four substantive voices agreed; no one disputed it). Dedicated R3F a11y packages are stale.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Mirror the node list, selected module and key metrics in a visually-hidden HTML layer with live regions. Full keyboard navigation of canvas nodes and camera bookmarks. Do not rely on @react-three/a11y (last published 2022).

principles.principle: Licence hygiene decides what ships. AGPL (xeokit, Theatre Studio) and LGPL WASM (OCCT builds) carry obligations; MPL-2.0 (web-ifc) is file-level; Zlib, MIT, Apache-2.0 and CC0 are easy.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Decide the platform's own licence first (open question for the team). Keep a THIRD_PARTY licence table in the repo; ship LGPL WASM with source/relink notice; never bundle AGPL code unless the platform is AGPL.

principles.principle: Agent-generated art is slow and token-hungry: Anatomy's documented example took about 1 h 54 min, the author calls token use substantial, and two runs differ. Time-box it.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Allow at most a few hero figures from anatomy/hairline-create, each with a spend cap. Use Hairline's static package and tokens for routine UI art. Cache generated figures in the repo so they are never regenerated per user.

principles.principle: Prefer in-browser WASM over native Python on student Windows machines. Smart App Control can block unsigned OCP, CadQuery pip supports Python 3.9-3.12, and Node is not yet installed on the team machines.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Core runs in the browser with no native installs beyond Node LTS (v24 or v22 per nodejs.org listing). Any Python CAD stays optional behind a documented WSL/conda path and telemetry opt-out.

recommendations.decision: Adopt Vite + React 19.3 + TypeScript + three 0.186.1 + R3F 9.8.2 + drei 10.7.9 with the WebGL2 renderer, all pinned in a lockfile. Install Node LTS (24 or 22) first.
recommendations.rationale: Compatible peer ranges today: R3F needs react >=19 <19.4, postprocessing needs three <0.187, That Open needs three >=0.182. Pinning avoids upgrade breakage before 13 Nov. Claude handles this ecosystem well, saving tokens.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: R3F v10 alpha/WebGPU-first (pre-release, N8AO and postprocessing are WebGL-only); Babylon.js (ecosystem mismatch); raw three.js without R3F (more boilerplate).

recommendations.decision: Default look 'Clay and Hairline': matte white massing, drei Edges plus fat lines (about 1 to 1.5 px), N8AO at half resolution, SMAA, tone mapping, Outlines for hover, one accent colour. Provide switchable presets: Section (ortho plus stencil caps), Exploded axon, Analysis (false colour), Diagram (halftone/Kuwahara).
recommendations.rationale: Matches the instructor-shared tools' restraint (thin lines, one accent, light first) and uses cheap existing components. Presets keep each view focused on one task.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Photoreal PBR as default (heavy on laptops, distracts from analysis); full-scene screen-space edge detection (extra pass, noisy).

recommendations.decision: Use Manifold (manifold-3d 3.5.4) in a worker as the massing and boolean kernel; expose nodes for extrude (twist/taper), union/subtract, slice-to-area, volume, project and section split.
recommendations.rationale: Covers tower massing, GFA per floor and sections with one 2.8 MB-unpacked package; guaranteed-manifold booleans reduce debugging. Replicad/occt-wasm only as optional v1 detail modules.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: opencascade.js (stale since 2023); JSCAD (mesh CSG, no robustness advantage found); three-bvh-csg (experimental, needs manifold inputs, README points to Manifold for robustness); CadQuery in Pyodide (not in package list).

recommendations.decision: Importers: .3dm via three Rhino3dmLoader with local rhino3dm 8.35 wasm; IFC via web-ifc 0.0.78 in a worker; OBJ/glTF via three loaders. Add That Open components (clipper, plans) in v1. For SketchUp and Revit, ask users to export IFC or glTF now; consider Speckle connectors on the roadmap.
recommendations.rationale: All are MIT/MPL/Apache and run client-side, so no server cost. A verified browser reader for .skp was not found in this pass.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: xeokit (AGPL-3.0); Speckle viewer as the viewport (Viewer 2 cannot render current bundles without a bridge, Viewer 3 unreleased).

recommendations.decision: Implement text-to-massing, not free-form text-to-CAD: LLM outputs JSON for typed massing nodes, validated by Manifold, with render-and-check feedback and editable assumptions. Install earthtojake/text-to-cad as a developer Claude Code plugin only for small details. Zoo API only as an optional flagged integration later.
recommendations.rationale: Published text-to-CAD results come from single mechanical parts (69.3% exact match at best); JSON generation is cheaper and verifiable. text-to-cad has no architecture-scale examples and Windows SAC issues.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Free-form LLM-to-CadQuery in core; Zoo Text-to-CAD as a dependency (hosted engine, credit cost, no benchmarks); cad0 (7B-class mechanical-part model).

recommendations.decision: Sun and shadow: SunCalc (wrapped and unit-tested) drives a CSM directional light in WebGL; drei Sky for the sky; accumulate soft ground shadows only when still. Compute shadow hours analytically by BVH raycasts from grid points, not from rendered pixels.
recommendations.rationale: Analysis must be reproducible and citable while the visual shadow is only illustrative. CSM is WebGL-only today; SunLight is WebGPU-documented. takram atmosphere is beta and its API is being rewritten.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: SunLight addon now (WebGPU only); takram atmosphere now; AccumulativeShadows as the analysis source (planar ground catcher, not an analysis tool).

recommendations.decision: Performance budget: frameloop demand, PerformanceMonitor-driven DPR, instancing, BVH picking, N8AO half-res, Low/Medium/High tiers with a visible quality toggle, and a smoke test on the weakest team laptop before 13 Nov.
recommendations.rationale: Student laptops vary; vendor figures (N8AO 2x-4x, BVH 500 rays at 60 fps) are unverified here, so measure. Adaptive quality keeps the tool responsive and focused.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Fixed high quality for everyone; WebGPU path-tracing for the live view (three-gpu-pathtracer needs WebGPU and long convergence).

recommendations.decision: Aesthetic system: adopt Hairline's token ladder and the @lucasmarkes/hairline package for module cards, empty states and onboarding; generate at most a few hero figures with hairline-create or anatomy with a spend cap and cached outputs.
recommendations.rationale: Gives a consistent calm visual language cheaply; hero art is expensive (about 2 h agent time per Anatomy example). Hairline's interaction rules keep motion purposeful, not manipulative.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Per-module generated illustrations (token cost, inconsistent output); Theatre.js for motion (stalled, AGPL studio); animated attention-grabbing UI.

recommendations.decision: Add a compatibility and licence file: version pins (three below 0.187, react below 19.4), a monthly upgrade check, and a licence table. Block AGPL dependencies in CI and ship LGPL WASM with source notices.
recommendations.rationale: Several peer ranges are tight and licences differ (MPL, LGPL, AGPL, CC0 vs npm ISC for N8AO). A small file prevents rework and legal surprises for an open-source platform.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Floating versions with caret ranges; deciding licences at release time.

recommendations.decision: Treat hairline, anatomy and text-to-cad as dev-time and design resources, not runtime dependencies: install their skills for the team, read their rules, and verify with Xun which repositories she meant, since none sits in her xunliuDesign account.
recommendations.rationale: They are third-party MIT repos, very new (Anatomy created 2026-10-08) and fast-changing. Using them as references saves time without lock-in, and confirms we have the right projects.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Vendoring their code into the platform; waiting on upstream updates for core features.

flags.claim: opencascade.js is the maintained way to run OpenCascade in the browser.
flags.correction: Repo last pushed 2023-08-15; npm latest 1.1.1 is dated 2020-09-27 (OCCT 7.6.2). Use replicad-opencascadejs 1.1.0 (2026-09-04) or occt-wasm 5.7.1 (OCCT 8.0.1, 2026-10-12).
flags.detail: Sources: GitHub repo page, npm registry, occt-wasm README.

flags.claim: CadQuery or build123d can run in the browser through Pyodide.
flags.correction: Neither cadquery, build123d nor OCP appear in the Pyodide 314.0.7 package list; CadQuery README says pip supports Python 3.9-3.12 only.
flags.detail: Browser B-rep needs a WASM OCCT build (replicad, occt-wasm). No verified Pyodide route found in this pass.

flags.claim: Zoo text-to-CAD is open-source and can run locally.
flags.correction: The modeling-app is MIT, but its README says the 3D view streams from Zoo's hosted geometry engine; Text-to-CAD/Zookeeper is a hosted service drawing on monthly usage credits.
flags.detail: Zoo's pages give no benchmarks or error rates. KCL licence and local execution not confirmed.

flags.claim: Theatre.js is an actively maintained open-source animation stack.
flags.correction: Public repo last pushed 2024-08-14; README says development moved to a private repo for v1.0; npm 0.7.2 is from 2024-05-19; @theatre/studio is AGPL-3.0.
flags.detail: Core is Apache-2.0; only core ships in a bundle.

flags.claim: xeokit can be embedded in an open-source or permissive project at no cost or constraint.
flags.correction: xeokit-sdk is AGPL-3.0; closed or proprietary use needs a commercial licence from Creoox.
flags.detail: Fine only if the platform adopts AGPL-3.0.

flags.claim: The Speckle viewer can display any current Speckle model out of the box.
flags.correction: Speckle docs say Viewer 2 cannot render current parquet-bundle model versions without a bridge, and Viewer 3 is unreleased.

flags.claim: three.js SunLight (r186) gives cascaded sun shadows in the WebGL renderer, and N8AO works with WebGPU.
flags.correction: SunLight docs show setup for WebGPURenderer only; use the CSM addon for WebGL. N8AO README says it is not yet WebGPU-compatible.
flags.detail: Sources: threejs.org SunLight and CSM docs; N8AO README.

flags.claim: rhino3dm.js can perform booleans or meshing of Breps locally.
flags.correction: README lists geometry containers and .3dm I/O only; advanced operations go through Rhino Compute.
flags.detail: Whether Breps without stored render meshes display via Rhino3dmLoader was not tested.

flags.claim: Vendor performance figures: three-mesh-bvh (500 rays on 80k polygons at 60 fps), N8AO half-res 2x-4x speedup, Manifold faster than OpenSCAD, web-ifc native speeds, Fragments millions of elements in seconds.
flags.correction: All are author claims with no test setup; none was measured on student laptops.
flags.detail: Measure on the weakest team laptop before fixing quality tiers.
